text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Australia's biggest retailer Coles Myer Ltd exceeded market expectations yesterday by coming out of one of its worst periods with a 40.7 per cent increase in interim profits to A$273.6 million. Investors said the result - which included a A$44.6 million profit from a A$585 million in property sales - justified the recent increase in Coles Myer's share price. Page 1.

A refusal by the Federal Government last night to exempt the front-running consortium headed by Lend Lease and Brambles Industries from its foreign ownership rules has left the consortium's future in the A$3 billion airports privatisation uncertain. Fearing it would set a precedent for the sale of Telstra by giving way to the Brambles-Lend Lease partnership, the Government yesterday would not back down on its 49 per cent limit for overseas ownership of the airports. Page 4.

Entertainment giant Village Roadshow has called on shareholders to fund A$120 million to move from a 53 per cent stake in Austereo to full ownership. The fund-raising follows a A$216 million placement to institutions last year and a A$230 million finance package from ANZ last month. Page 31.

RTZ-CRA has ended five-year legal action over CRA's takeover of Kalimantan Gold NL and production forecasts made at the time, settling out of court on litigation over the Kelian mine with five Australian companies associated with Plutonic Resources Ltd, Resolute Ltd, and
FAI Insurances Ltd. Page 31.

The proposed A$200 million merger of St Barbara with Mt Leyshon Gold Mines, launched on Wednesday, has seen St Barbara offering scrip for Mt Leyshon to create a 350,000 ounce-a-year gold producer. Ross Atkins, a shareholder involved in a bitter boardroom struggle at St Barbara, claims the move is a great deal for Normandy but pays no thought for St Barbara Mines' shareholders. Page 31.

Kerry Stokes' Seven Network Ltd and Optus Vision partners yesterday agreed to extend their settlement talks by a further 24 hours and the control of the cable-TV company with a cash settlement could come as early as Sunday. Payment to Seven is expected t be linked to a re-evaluation of Seven's contribution to Optus Vision's pay-TV sports programming arm. Page 31.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Coles Myer Ltd yesterday announced a 40 per cent rise in interim net profit and forecast a similar growth in the second half. Total sales revenue increased 5.4 per cent in a result primarily achieved through turnaround performances by the Myer Grace Bros and K mart divisions. Profit after tax and abnormals for the six months to January 26 was 40.7 per cent better than the previous half, a result exceeding the half-year performance of direct supermarket competitor Woolworths Ltd. Page 21.

Shell Australia has earmarked A$170 million this year for exploration in the greater North West Shelf amid reports that its recent Cornea discovery north-west of Broome in Western Australia could hold as much as 500 million barrels of oil. The Cornea discovery cold be Australia's biggest single oil find outside of Bass Strait and would require upwards of A$1 billion to develop. Page 21.

Federal Finance Minister John Fahey yesterday named the seven global co-ordinators or lead managers of the A$30 billion Telstra float. JB Were and Son in Australia, ABN Amro Rothschild in Europe and Credit Suisse First Boston in America are joint global managers, while Ord Minnett, Goldman Sachs, Macquarie Bank, Daiwa and Securities and Deutsche Morgan Grenfell join them as lead managers. Page 21.

Reports swept through the market yesterday that a long-awaited rationalisation of the pay-TV industry was imminent. Shares in satellite operator Australis Media Ltd rose by three cents and Optus Communications shareholder Mayne Nickless Ltd shares rose 13 cents as sources close to the main industry players confirmed talks were proceeding on several fronts including possible sharing of programming and methods of delivery. Page 21.

A jump in unemployment has kept hopes of an interest rate cut alive while the benchmark November 2006 bond yield fell 1 basis point to 7.80 per cent and the Australian dollar slipped to US79.20 cents from US79.43 cents amid profit taking. Employment fell by 7200 as a 17,000 increase in part-time work was offset by a 24,400 decline in full-time jobs. Page 22.

Amalgamated Holdings Ltd has reported a 15 per cent rise in interim after-tax earnings amid news the entertainment and leisure group is near to signing its first offshore deals for its hotel and cinema divisions. Amalgamated plans to open a
10-cinema compex in Dubai later this calendar year and expects to have more than 300 screens operating locally by the end of the financial year. Page 23.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

In a period described by retailers as the worst in a decade, Coles Myer has lifted its profitability levels back to those of 1994-95 by raising net profit 23.1 per cent to A$229 million in the latest half-year. The profit increase has been attributed to internal adjustments, the lack of deep discounting, and better
timing of markdowns than any unusual increase in customer numbers. Page 25.

The Federal Government is to consider the use of the instalment sale method to entice small investors into the A$10 billion-plus sharemarket listing of Telstra. The method was successfully used in last year's Commonwealth Bank float, with Finance Minister John Fahey yesterday describing the process as an attractive approach. Page 25.

The 2.3 million policy holders in AMP Society are in for an anxious few months as they wait to discover whether they will be eligible for shares in AMP's float. An exclusive briefing - The D-Word -will give some insight into share allocation. The document contains comprehensive guidelines on which policies qualify and how transfers affect entitlements. Page 25.

Bankers Trust Australia has suffered a three per cent drop in net profit to A$234.7 million for 1996 in what appears to be a trend of declining profitability. BTA managing director Rob Ferguson described 1996 as "perhaps the toughest year" for the

Santos managing director Ross Alder said yesterday Australia's oil and gas industry's 'new dimension' could be attributed to greater exploration activity and the regular arrival on the market of quality assets. Adler also said that at a time when his group was set for major expansion, the maturing of the industry, emergence of new players, and deregulation of the gas industry were adding more depth to the field. Page 29.
THE AGE
company and pointed to the A$340 pre-tax profit as a better measure of performance while blaming the latter on increased tax rates. Page 27.

Talks between the Seven Network and fellow shareholders in Optus Vision continued yesterday as Seven gave its partners an extra 24 hours to offer an acceptable peace deal to end their court battle. The case threatens to overturn the cable group's ownership structure, yet some parties are predicting the talks could result in a settlement being reached today to coincide with an Optus Communications board meeting. Page 27.

The Federal Government yesterday announced three investment houses as lead brokers for the A$10 billion partial float of Telstra - one of the world's biggest capital raisings. The brokers - Melbourne based J.B Were & Son, American investment house Credit Suisse First Boston and Anglo-Dutch partnership ABN AMRO Rothschild - will be responsible for the Australian component of the float, the American float sales and European trade. Page B1.

In a period other retailers describe as the worst in 10 years, Coles Myer has staged a strong earnings recovery by lifting net profits 23.1 per cent to A$229 million in the latest half year figures. The improvement - which lifts profit levels back to the ecord amounts of 1994-95 - is due more to internal adjustments, a lack of deep discounting and better timing of markdowns than any increase in customer numbers. Page B1.

The prospect of the A$370 million proposed merger of St Barbara Mines and Mount Leyshon Gold Mines becoming a new gold arm for Robert Champion de Crespigny's Normandy Mining yesterday added an extra dimension to the joining of the mining groups. The identfication of a resource of more than 800,000 ounces at St Barbara's Cuddlingwarra gold field has sharpened market attention on the possibility of a quick development of the field. Page B2.

Entertainment group Village Roadshow is seeking to up its stake in the commercial FM radio network Austereo by offering A$192.3 million for the 47.2 per cent of the network it does not already own. Village, which currently owns 52.8 per cent of Austereo, says the bid is worth equivalent to A$2.35 a share and will be financed by a placement of new shares to institutions to be underwritten by ANZ Securities. Page B3.

After reporting a rise the December-half net profit to A$29.3 million from a previous A$9.6 million, Telecasters North Queensland is well positioned to become a proxy listed vehicle for the Ten television network. TNQ company chairman George Chapman said esterday that within four weeks TNQ would convert to a single purpose company at the completion of its divesting of all but its 18.2 million shares in the television group. TNQ currently holds a 40 per cent voting interest and a 20 per cent economic interest in Ten. Page B3.

The trend of declining profitability has continued for Bankers Trust Australia after the group posted a three per cent fall in net profit to A$234.7 million for 1996. BTA managing director Rob Ferguson blamed the disappointing result on increased tax rate and indicated the company's A$340 million pre-tax profit as a better guide to performance. Page B3.
